name: Luvadaxistat
summary: Luvadaxistat is an experimental drug that works as a D-amino acid oxidase (DAAO) inhibitor and is supposed to increase NMDA receptor functionality. It is developed to treat Friedrich ataxia and negative symptoms of schizophrenia. As of September 2024, it is in phase 2 clinical trials for schizophrenia, no recent development has been reported for ataxia, and the drug has been discontinued for Friedreich's ataxia.

pharmacology.text: Luvadaxistat (INN, USAN; NBI-1065844, TAK-831) is an experimental drug that works as a D-amino acid oxidase (DAAO) inhibitor and is supposed to increase NMDA receptor functionality.

uses.text: It is developed to treat Friedrich ataxia and negative symptoms of schizophrenia. As of September 2024, it is in phase 2 clinical trials for schizophrenia, no recent development has been reported for ataxia, and the drug has been discontinued for Friedreich's ataxia.

fact.en: The enzyme it blocks, D-amino acid oxidase, breaks down D-serine, a mirror-image amino acid that the brain uses to help switch on NMDA receptors.
fact.zh: 它所抑制的 D-胺基酸氧化酶會分解 D-絲胺酸，這是一種「鏡像」胺基酸，大腦用它來幫助啟動 NMDA 受體。
fact.zhHans: 它所抑制的 D-胺基酸氧化酶会分解 D-丝胺酸，这是一种「镜像」胺基酸，大脑用它来帮助启动 NMDA 受体。
